text.p: Western Resources Inc, which holds a 24.3 percent stake in ADT Ltd, said it will oppose Republic Industries Inc's plan to buy the security firm.
"We are opposing that transaction. We believe that Republic stock is much too volatile to give Western any real benefit," said Western spokeswoman Michel Philipp.
Western is not divulging its strategy to oppose the transaction, Philipp said.

However, she noted that one possible method would be for Western to acquire a larger chunk of ADT stock. In fact, Western received government permission earlier this month to acquire between 25 and 50 percent of ADT common shares.
Shares of Western were up 1/8 at 29.
Philipp said the company's opposition to the proposed merger was contained in a filing made to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on September 13.

Republic announced in July that it planned to buy ADT in a stock transaction valued at $5 billion. But the transaction has caused immense concern on Wall Street because shares of Republic, which hovered at $29 a share when the deal was struck in July, sank below $20 just a few weeks later.
Republic shares were up 5/8 to 27-7/8 in early trade. Shares of ADT were unchanged at 20-1/2.
